errors: No numeric targets committed (LCP 2.5 s cited only as a reference); INP never named
Defer of non-critical JS proposed with no specific warning that it can break checkout or builder widgets
R4-A.why: Measurement-led plan that splits server from browser time, branches on the result, gates the page cache with a two-browser cart test and treats hosting as a trialled, costed decision; weaker only on firm targets and the JS-optimisation warning.

errors: Changes are re-measured per group, not one at a time, and no rollback step or off-peak rule is stated
Hosting move carries a price but no migration risk or cutover plan; a small VPS is offered without noting the lack of a sysadmin
Phase 1 runs eight workstreams in one week regardless of what the TTFB split shows, so the branch is stated but not really followed
PHP 20-30% gain presented as a general figure
R4-B.why: Broad and technically correct with numeric targets, cache exclusions, cart fragments and a 28-day field-data note, but it reads as a complete checklist with weak change control and no way back on a live store.

errors: No numeric targets (deferred to after the baseline); INP not named
No warning that JS delay/defer can break checkout or builder widgets
Hosting cost left unquantified
R4-C.why: Clear measure-then-fix plan with a go/no-go gate for the page cache, plugin protection by default, a careful migration and a revert rule, missing only firm targets and the JS-optimisation caveat.

errors: Freezing product edits during the DNS switch does not stop orders being split between the two hosts, so the claim that no orders are lost is not backed
Step 4 bundles PHP upgrade, plugin deactivation and database clean-up under a one-change-at-a-time rule
No note that field data lags about 28 days
R4-D.why: Catches every trap with concrete commands, cookie-level cache exclusions, numeric targets, a gated hosting move with rollback and a conditional two-template rebuild, with only small slips in the migration detail.

errors: Tells the reader to turn on HPOS with no plugin-compatibility check
Relies on the cache plugin's default WooCommerce exclusions rather than verifying them before go-live (the two-browser test sits only in the risk list)
No rollback step, no off-peak rule, and business-critical plugins are not named or protected
Migration described as a day or two with no cost or cutover safeguards
R4-E.why: Well ordered from cheap to costly with numeric targets, per-change re-measurement and the right front-end specifics, but safety and plugin protection are thin and hosting risk is understated.

errors: Promises a typical drop from 6 s to 2.5-3.5 s after Phase 1 with no data
Phases are fixed regardless of the TTFB reading, so the split does not steer the plan
Query Monitor installed 'temporarily' without saying staging only; no one-change-at-a-time rule, no test order and no rollback
Critical CSS, unused-CSS removal, defer and minify proposed together in one phase; business-critical plugins not protected; migration risk absent
R4-F.why: Comprehensive and mostly correct, with good cache exclusions and targets, but it is a generic phased checklist with weak branching, loose change control and an unsupported result estimate.

errors: No committed numeric target (2.5 s LCP is only a reference); checkout is not in the measured URL set and INP is not named
Says a host move can be reversed by keeping the old account, without addressing orders placed on the new host meanwhile
Nonce lifetime stated as 24 hours (hedged); the usable window is 12-24 hours, so a cache lifetime just under 24 hours can still fail
Business-critical plugins (payment, shipping, ERP) are not explicitly protected; cart fragments not mentioned
R4-G.why: The strongest safety design of the set (cache gate and abort rule, variant-pricing question, staging e-mails off, failed-order monitoring, deactivate rather than delete) on a properly branched, measured plan, held back slightly by no firm targets and thin plugin protection.

errors: Autoload SQL filters only on 'yes' and 'on', missing the 'auto' and 'auto-on' values used since WordPress 6.6, so it under-counts
Third-party scripts (pixels, chat, review widgets) are not covered, and the JS warning is limited to a functional check
Asserts that asset unloading usually recovers most of the page builder's cost, which is not supported
The 'high TTFB everywhere' row pairs plugin deactivation with a PHP upgrade
R4-H.why: Tight, measured and reversible, with tested backup restore, a test order after every change, explicit targets and the most honest migration rollback (orders on the new host must be re-entered), but it skips third-party scripts.

errors: States that shared hosting is very likely too small and that it would move, before any measurement, and calls it the only fix for a slow checkout
Offers a small VPS with no mention of who would administer it
Only TTFB is named as a metric; no rollback, no one-change-at-a-time rule; business-critical plugins unprotected
Critical CSS and deferred loading proposed with no warning that they can break checkout
R4-I.why: Correct order of work and safe cache exclusions in a compact plan, but hosting is assumed rather than decided from the data and the change-control and plugin-protection detail is thin.
